stories.new_fact: States United Democracy Center and Grant Witness released Lost Funds, a tracker estimating up to $177 billion in federal grants cut, frozen, delayed, or otherwise disrupted since Trump's second term began.
stories.new_takeaway: Grant recipients need award-level status tracking and client communications because the risk is cash flow, payroll and service continuity, not only headline spending politics.
stories.why_now: The tracker was released Wednesday and turns scattered grant-cut disputes into a searchable operating map.
stories.previous_coverage: Not covered in the previous seven scripts; FEMA staffing and federal election administration were adjacent but different.
stories.uncertainty: The tracker depends on federal spending records and ongoing litigation; totals may change as agencies and courts act.
stories.watch: Watch for court orders, agency letters releasing frozen funds, or service providers reporting payroll or program cuts.

stories.new_fact: Columbus City Schools earned 2.5 stars, up from 2 stars, while early literacy and graduation remain at one star and the district faces another $50 million in cuts.
stories.new_takeaway: The report card should guide budget prioritization toward durable early-literacy and graduation interventions rather than treating the half-star gain as sufficient momentum.
stories.why_now: The state report card was released Tuesday and local outlets updated the district breakdown Tuesday night.
stories.previous_coverage: Previous scripts covered Columbus schools' social-media litigation but not the 2026 report card.
stories.uncertainty: The graduation component uses older data through summer 2025, while the district's class of 2026 graduation rate is newer.
stories.watch: Watch whether the 84.6% class of 2026 graduation rate lifts next year's state accountability score and how the board protects literacy work during cuts.

stories.new_fact: MBA weekly data showed the average contract rate for a 30-year fixed mortgage at 6.97% for the week ending September 11, with total applications down 4.1%, refinances down 8.8%, and purchases down 0.8%.
stories.new_takeaway: Lenders should triage refinance follow-up by net benefit and servicing-retention logic while refreshing purchase qualifications exposed to near-7% pricing.
stories.why_now: The weekly MBA figures were released Wednesday morning and update yesterday's seven-percent purchase-file story with fresh application behavior.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent episodes covered daily seven-percent quotes, Freddie Mac's weekly survey, and preapproval refreshes; this segment uses new MBA application data and a different pipeline-triage takeaway.
stories.uncertainty: The original MBA article was not exposed in search results, so the figures were taken from a live market data service citing MBA and supported by MBA/Freddie context.
stories.watch: Watch whether the Fed decision lowers long yields enough to reprice locks or whether refi follow-up remains highly selective.

stories.new_fact: Business Insider reported Goldman Sachs investment-banking co-head Kim Posnett's description of AI use for research, earnings-call summarization and junior-banker preparation, while no task-level performance metric was disclosed.
stories.new_takeaway: The banking question shifts from adoption to analyst-training design: AI can speed research, but banks still need human correction records and a training path that preserves judgment.
stories.why_now: The article was published Wednesday and supports a new Goldman row in the AI banking ledger.
stories.previous_coverage: Previous AI-in-banking segments covered Schwab, Pockit, Rogo, FIS, Truist, OpenAI financial services and JPMorganChase; Goldman was not a recent full segment.
stories.uncertainty: The source is reputable reporting and executive commentary, not an audit, customer disclosure, regulator finding or earnings-call metric.
stories.watch: Watch for Goldman or another large bank disclosing adoption scope, review controls, or measured research-prep productivity with error rates.
stories.ledger_row_changed: Goldman Sachs | lanes 5, 6, 7 | new production row for investment-banking research, earnings-call summarization, client-preparation and junior-banker productivity workflows; evidence rank reputable reporting; no task-level metric disclosed.

stories.new_fact: AP reported that Amodei proposed ongoing employee-like access for independent frontier-lab evaluators, Anthropic is committing to it, and Altman said OpenAI would follow.
stories.new_takeaway: The frontier safety debate now has a concrete mechanism to evaluate: buyer trust depends on evaluator independence, public standards and escalation rights, not the mere existence of auditors.
stories.why_now: The AP report was published Wednesday and advances the prior slowdown debate with implementation details.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent scripts covered frontier slowdown warnings, China's response and China model catch-up; this segment avoids repeating those conclusions and focuses on embedded evaluator mechanics.
stories.uncertainty: No benchmark or independent replication is involved; critics question independence, antitrust risk and concentration of power.
stories.watch: Watch whether labs publish evaluator scopes, standards, findings or escalation paths before the September 24 AI governance meeting.
stories.frontier_bar: Policy that binds labs directly, plus safety and security evaluation; no measured model capability claim.

stories.new_fact: AP reported global stocks higher ahead of an expected Fed hike, a 10-year Treasury around 5%, Brent at $108.34, U.S. crude at $104.86, and an expected quarter-point hike to about 3.9%.
stories.new_takeaway: Markets and mortgage desks care less about the quarter point than whether Warsh's statement lowers or raises the inflation premium in long yields.
stories.why_now: The Fed decision is due Wednesday after the episode cutoff, so the morning setup is the actionable development.
stories.previous_coverage: Recent markets segments covered Fed setup and oil pressure; today's version is compact and tied to the Fed-day long-yield test.
stories.uncertainty: The actual Fed decision and press conference were not available at cutoff.
stories.watch: Watch the statement, projections and 10-year Treasury reaction after the Fed announcement.

stories.new_takeaway: Listeners should keep flexibility for pickup, job sites and evening practices because scattered storms may still disrupt local travel.
stories.why_now: Weather changes same-day planning for Columbus-area listeners.
stories.previous_coverage: Routine weather appeared in all prior episodes; today's line uses current NWS timing only.
stories.uncertainty: Scattered convection can miss some neighborhoods while disrupting others.
stories.watch: Recheck radar before afternoon and evening cross-town travel.
